requirement_text.REQ-044: Port the core value types and top-level dispatch of src/engine/transition.zig's transition() as a pure Letflow module -- no Ecto.Repo call, no I/O, no clock read. Builds lib/letflow/engine/{token.ex,instance_state.ex,transition.ex}. Determinism is load-bearing (EE-02 AC2, XC-04 kernel determinism): identical inputs always produce identical outputs, demonstrated by an explicit test rather than asserted. An unknown/unrecognised event type returns an error result, and a state whose token sits on a node_id absent from the snapshot graph returns an error result naming the offending node_id -- neither raises or crashes. A token entering a HUMAN_TASK node adds that node to pending_task_nodes, while tokens entering START, END, EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY and PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes do not -- each of the five node-type cases has its own explicit test. The moduledoc states explicitly that Zig's std.json.ObjectMap allocator-ownership contract is deliberately not ported. The module reuses REQ-028's existing graph structs from lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex rather than defining a second copy.

task.description: WF-02 Step 3 (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md 'Step 3 — Test design'). This requirement has real application-executable surface (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex etc.) so the scope test says YES -- proceed with full test design. Read lib/letflow/design/req044-transition-kernel.md and the 3 implementation files. Write test/specs/REQ-044.md (requirement text, test cases, why each exists) and test code under test/letflow/engine/ (e.g. transition_test.exs, instance_state_test.exs -- follow the existing test/letflow/ directory convention, check test/letflow/definitions/ for the established style). Since determinism is the load-bearing property (per the requirement text), include a StreamData property test for it, following the property-test convention already established elsewhere in this project (e.g. process_instance_test.exs) if applicable to this pure-function shape.
